scope: Opt-in evidence-based retrieval of earlier numeric outcome memories under unannounced A -> B -> A rule reversals; simulated observations only, no new environment interfaces or automatic policy promotion.
freeze: This file must be committed before learner or evaluation implementation. Once evaluated, both cohorts become inspected.
environment: ObservableWorld route (A) and route-reversed (B), existing hand-authored two-number action features and public before-action-after outcome.
observation_actor: An independent seeded random actor selects exactly one legal action in each disposable episode; archive the public outcome. The learning algorithm cannot choose training actions. Count harmful actor interventions separately. The untrained random TEST baseline has a separate deterministic per-episode choice and uses no training evidence.

retrieval.scoring_exclusion: Candidate block must end at or before the start of the latest 12 training observations: never score a block on events used to train it.

checkpoint: Exact event replay, SHA-256 integrity, no phase labels in learner records, immutable read-only evaluation, support restart midstream.
success_criteria: Return-to-A success improves over both cumulative and recent-32 after only 12 new observations; B is not materially worse than recent-32; results reproducible in both frozen cohorts. No promotion if gates fail.
caveats: Known route/reversed numeric feature rules in a single simulator, not genuinely new environment families
Block segmentation and 12-observation retrieval context are hand-engineered inductive biases
Training actions are potentially harmful even when generated by an external simulator actor
No source authenticity or protection against collusive fabrication
Selection sees actual outcomes of the 12 return-stage simulator actions, so this is fast relearning, not zero-shot
No autonomous goals, identity, consciousness, AthenZ/Synveil integration, or real-world authority
Never merge or promote the draft automatically
